record.paper_title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
record.original_question: For every 3-connected cubic graph G, does there exist a blue-red vertex coloring whose blue induced subgraph B has maximum degree at most 1 and whose red induced subgraph R satisfies some weakened replacement for the failed crumby-coloring red conditions, namely minimum degree at least 1 and no path with 3 edges? Equivalently, what relaxation of the conditions imposed on the red induced subgraph R guarantees that such a blue-red coloring always exists for every 3-connected cubic graph?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.1 What relaxation of the conditions on R guarantees that such a coloring of a 3-connected cubic graph always exists?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A crumby coloring of a graph $G$ is a partition of $V(G)$ into two classes, called blue and red, such that the subgraph $B$ induced by the blue vertices has maximum degree at most $1$ (i.e. $B$ is a disjoint union of isolated vertices and isolated edges) and the subgraph $R$ induced by the red vertices has minimum degree at least $1$ and contains no path with $3$ edges (i.e. every connected component of $R$ has at most $3$ vertices and at least one edge). It was conjectured that every 3-connected cubic graph admits a crumby coloring, but this conjecture is false: infinite families of 3-connected cubic graphs without any crumby coloring exist.

Determine a relaxation of the conditions imposed on the red induced subgraph $R$ that is sufficient to guarantee the following statement: for every 3-connected cubic graph $G$, there exists a partition of $V(G)$ into a blue class and a red class such that the blue induced subgraph $B$ has maximum degree at most $1$ and the red induced subgraph $R$ satisfies the relaxed conditions (which should still imply $\delta(R)\ge 1$ and forbid the existence of arbitrarily long paths in $R$, in the spirit of weakening "no path with $3$ edges").
artifact.status_search_result: The original crumby-coloring conjecture of Thomassen for 3-connected cubic graphs was disproved by Bellitto, Klimošová, Merker, Witkowski and Yuditsky, who constructed an infinite family of counterexamples. The question of what suitable relaxation of the conditions on the red induced subgraph would restore a guarantee of existence for every 3-connected cubic graph is posed as an open problem and does not appear to have been resolved.

status_evidence.title: Crumby colorings — Red-blue vertex partition of subcubic graphs regarding a conjecture of Thomassen
status_evidence.snippet: Introduces crumby colorings and studies Thomassen's conjecture that every 3-connected cubic graph admits one.
status_evidence.claim: Defines crumby colorings and the conjecture for 3-connected cubic graphs.

status_evidence.title: Counterexamples to Thomassen's Conjecture on Decomposition of Cubic Graphs
status_evidence.snippet: Bellitto et al. construct infinite families of 3-connected cubic graphs with no crumby coloring.
status_evidence.claim: The original conjecture is false, motivating the question of a correct relaxation.

status_evidence.title: Open problems of the 32nd Workshop on Cycles and Colourings
status_evidence.snippet: Lists the problem of identifying a relaxation of the red conditions guaranteeing existence for every 3-connected cubic graph.
status_evidence.claim: The relaxation problem is posed as open.
